title: Ericsson and YAS Madagascar collaborate to advance young people’s digital skills
summary: Ericsson and YAS Madagascar bring digital skills training in 5G, AI and IoT to university students.
body_markdown:
Ericsson (NASDAQ: ERIC) and YAS Madagascar, a subsidiary of Yas Group, launched Ericsson Educate 21st century technologies for university students across Madagascar. The collaboration will empower students with future-ready digital skills and help build a pool of talent qualified in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM).


The initiative aligns with Madagascar’s national digital strategy, the Plan Stratégique du Numérique (PSN) 2023–2028, supporting its focus on digital capacity building and the development of skills needed for the country’s digital transformation.


The partnership addresses the growing demand for digital fluency by providing university students with access to relevant, high-quality training. Starting at the University of Antsiranana, the program will be available to students in computer science, telecommunications, and polytechnic faculties. The program will be delivered at YAS-sponsored IT Labs on university campuses, with plans to expand to more universities across the country until 2028.


Ericsson Educate 21st century technologies offers an interactive, mobile-friendly digital learning platform. It equips learners with practical skills in key technologies such as 5G, AI, IoT, automation, and cybersecurity through progressive, self-paced courses that culminate in real-world simulations.


Benoît Janin, Chief Executive Officer at YAS Madagascar says: "At YAS Madagascar, we see this partnership as an important step in helping equip Madagascar’s next generation with the skills they need to thrive in an increasingly digital world. Digital inclusion goes beyond connectivity; it is also about giving young people access to the knowledge, tools, and opportunities that will enable them to participate fully in the digital economy and contribute to Madagascar’s digital future."


Alain Maupin, Head of East and North Africa at Ericsson says: “Bringing Ericsson Educate 21st century technologies to university students in Madagascar is an important milestone in our collaboration with YAS Madagascar. By providing access to learning in key areas such as 5G, AI,the Internet of Things, data science and cyberscurity we are helping students build practical, future-ready skills while contributing to Madagascar’s national digital strategy and broader digital transformation ambitions.”


This partnership demonstrates a shared commitment to advancing digital inclusion in Africa. By equipping young people with the skills needed for 21st-century careers, Ericsson and YAS Madagascar are helping to accelerate the nation's digital transformation and create new professional pathways for its youth.
